children: Victory Capital announced a definitive Merger Agreement to acquire First Eagle through a two-step merger, with consideration comprising cash, new common shares equal to 4.9% of post-close shares, and Series B non-voting convertible preferred stock, subject to client consent and customary adjustments. To fund the deal and related costs, Victory secured up to $4.65 billion in committed financing from Bank of America and Royal Bank of Canada, including a $3.5 billion seven-year term loan, a $200 million five-year revolver, and a $950 million bridge facility. At closing, a Shareholder Agreement with Genstar will provide registration rights, board nomination rights tied to ownership, and a three-year lock-up and standstill to support post-merger stability. Closing remains subject to HSR clearance, other regulatory approvals, client consents, shareholder approvals for share issuance, and customary conditions.
